Split the match into ld_rs1/ld_rs2. load_use_hazard = (ld_rs1||ld_rs2) && !if_id_is_branch, so the final gate stays at 4 inputs {ld_nz, eq1, eq2, pd_br}. New outputs late_rs1/late_rs2 = ld_rs* && if_id_is_branch (data-only, never on the ID/EX CE).
Export pd_br && !kill (or pd_br computed from out.instr) as output pd_branch for the hazard unit. The BHT write port is unchanged, but it is now driven from MEM; update the header comment.
New inputs late_rs1/late_rs2. Latch late_rs1/late_rs2 and ld_nz = dec_mem_read && (instr[11:7] != 0) into ID/EX next to the prediction fields. reset/flush clear them.

New input kill (the MEM redirect). late = late_rs1||late_rs2 gates the EX redirect and misalign_branch. kill forces EX/MEM valid=0, ctrl='0 and late flags 0, and gates div_unit start (div_req &= !kill). Carry branch_cond, tgt_misalign, pred_taken, bht_ctr, alt_target and the late flags into EX/MEM. Remove the BHT update block and its bht_* outputs. Build the final redirect as one expression with mem_redirect folded in, and the target as (is_jalr && !mem_redirect) ? jalr_sum : (mem_redirect ? mem_target : alt_target), so the EX redirect/target paths gain no LUT level.

Late-branch verify. op1/op2 replace the late operand with the registered MEM/WB.read_data, then a six-way compare gives cond_late. replay = !MEM/WB.ctrl.reg_write (misaligned-load trap). redirect = late && (replay || (cond_late && !tgt_misalign) ^ pred_taken), target = replay ? pc : alt_target. MEM/WB captures corrected rs1_val/rs2_val and pc_next, is_illegal |= cond_late && tgt_misalign, and valid=0 on replay. Registered single BHT write port for all branches (cond = late ? cond_late : branch_cond; we = valid && is_branch && !(late && replay)). New outputs redirect, redirect_target, bht_we/bht_widx/bht_wdata.

Wire the MEM redirect/target into ex_stage (kill + target merge) so the combined redirect/redirect_target (MEM wins) reach if_stage and hazard_unit. Source the BHT write port from mem_stage. Wire pd_branch -> hazard_unit, late_rs1/late_rs2 -> id_stage and id_ex.ld_nz -> hazard_unit. Update the header comment.

Add directed cocotb tests. (a) A correctly predicted lw -> beq/bne on the loaded rs1 retires with no bubble. (b) A mispredicted load-dependent branch costs 2 bubbles and never commits a wrong-path SW or starts a wrong-path DIV. (c) A misaligned lw feeding a branch replays: the branch retires once, and rs1_rdata holds the old register value. (d) An lb/lh/lbu/lhu feeding all six branch ops on rs1, rs2 and both operands. (e) Load-dependent branches under random imem/dmem stalls give the same architectural RVFI stream as the no-stall run.

lesson: - 2026-09-26 hyp-20260926-003-r7s2 (regression, +12.66%): Re-applying r5s2's late load->branch verify on the r5s0 core landed its exact predicted cycles (3,406,859->3,278,562), and with ld_nz = mem_read && rd!=0 registered in ID/EX (so the load-use stall gate stayed 4-input) the load-use -> ID/EX CE path left the critical list and Fmax rose to the 189.14 MHz local median (seeds 199.5/173.4/189.1, all ending on ID/EX D inputs), which the scored fitness matched exactly; but the first build, which carried the raw 1-bit EX branch_cond into EX/MEM for MEM's BHT write, fell to 113-132 MHz on every seed with a 7.6-8.8 ns forward mux -> compare -> EX/MEM.branch_cond path that cone-depth estimates could not explain, and registering the 2-bit bht_upd instead (the compare only selects between two counter values precomputed from ID/EX flops, the same cone as the old EX-side BHT write) fixed it, so when a late compare's consumer moves a stage later, register a value the compare only selects between rather than a new flop of the raw compare bit, and 3-seed P&R every new EX->EX/MEM field before trusting it; it lost only to r7s0's LUT-RAM register file (+25.65%), so stack it on r7s0 next, where pd_branch and mem_redirect both feed that core's load-use/redirect -> ID/EX CE limiter.

title: Hide bus stalls on both sides: stall-only D-side store buffer + load cache, and a 4096-entry I-side replay store (netlist-identical to r7s0)
motivation:
I measured the current best (r7s0, 643.41 = 10 / 3,406,859 cycles x 219.2 MHz) on the
eval's own tools. Bracketed CoreMark cycles (test/cosim/build.sh, NRET=1, --bench):
  no stalls           3,191,647
  --istall only       3,216,666   (+25.0k)
  --dstall only       3,382,321   (+190.7k)
  --istall --dstall   3,406,859   (+215.2k, the scored run)
So 6.3% of the scored cycles are bus-refusal stalls. The FPGA Fmax bench
(core_bench_si.sv) ties io_imemReady and io_dmemReady to 1, so stall-only
structures cost nothing there if they fold away.

Where the other bubbles go (RVFI trace, 2,937,037 retirements, 487.6k bubbles):
- load-use ~205k: load->branch 135.5k, load->load pointer chase 59.3k, load->ALU only ~9k.
- branch mispredicts ~100k and JALR ~14k, each 1 cycle (redirect kills only F/D).
- bus stalls ~215k: the largest single bucket, and the only one that can be removed
  without touching the ready=1 netlist.

Fmax situation (my 3-seed P&R of r7s0 reproduces 219.20 / 228.68 / 209.07 MHz):
- seeds 1 and 3 end on IF BHT 64:1 read -> pred_raw -> alt_target mux -> ID/EX (4.56 / 4.78 ns)
- seed 2 ends on imem_data -> 4 decode LUTs -> ID/EX (4.37 ns)
Neither path touches the D-side or the replay store.

History. The D-side pair has twice delivered its predicted cycles, then lost to Fmax
re-rolls:
- r4s1: 3.70M -> 3.514M cycles, but 162 -> 152 MHz.
- r7s1: 3,406,859 -> 3,222,465 cycles on r5s0, which has the same cycle count as
  r7s0, but seeds 160/170/177 vs 171/174/175.
In both cases the netlist was "almost" folded: r7s1 went 5560 -> 5555 LUT4 and
2263 -> 2268 FF. That residue is what re-rolled P&R. This time the acceptance bar
is a bit-for-bit-equivalent bench netlist, so Fmax is inherited rather than rerolled.

The I side still leaves 25k istall cycles, because the 512-entry replay store
conflict-misses on CoreMark's 1,669 hot PCs. I swept RP_IDX_W on the current RTL
(only the localparam changed):
  RP_IDX_W  --istall only   both stalls
  9 (now)   3,216,666       3,406,859
  10        3,200,657       3,392,266
  11        3,196,433       3,387,916
  12        3,192,062       3,383,654   (-23.2k; istall-only is 415 cycles above the no-stall floor)
The store constant-folds away with imem_ready=1 (bench and formal wrapper_si both tie
it high), so its size is free in the scored netlist.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
One structural theme: make the pipeline tolerant of bus refusals on both ports, using
structures that are consulted ONLY on refused cycles. With the ready inputs tied to 1,
every new state bit has a constant D (equal to its reset value) or drives only dead
logic, so yosys removes it and the bench netlist is the r7s0 netlist.

A. I-side: RP_IDX_W 9 -> 12 in if_stage.sv
   - 4096 entries, index pc[13:2], tag pc[31:14]. Nothing else changes.
   - Measured: -23.2k cycles on the scored run.

B. D-side: re-apply r7s1's stall-only pair in mem_stage.sv
   The full spec is in log.jsonl under hyp-20260926-002-r7s1. Summary:
   - Terms:
       ld = mem_read && !mem_misalign
       st = mem_write && !mem_misalign
       cacheable = !alu_result[28]
       bus_free = dmem_ready && !sb_valid_q
       st_done = st && !sb_valid_q
       mem_ready = bus_free || (ld && cand_hit_q) || st_done
     hazard_unit: dmem_stall = !mem_ready && ex_mem_mem_op. Nothing else in
     hazard_unit changes.
   - 1-entry posted store buffer:
     - sb_valid_q <= !dmem_ready && (sb_valid_q || st).
     - Payload {addr, replicated wdata, wmask} is captured while !sb_valid_q.
     - The drain has bus priority.
     - dmem_addr/wdata/wen/ren are sb_valid_q ? sb_* (ren = 0) : today's EX/MEM-derived
       values. They are pure register functions with no io_dmemReady term.
     - It is FIFO, so UART bytes and the 0x10000100/104 markers keep program order.
   - Stall-only direct-mapped word load cache:
     - Arrays: dc_valid (reset), dc_tag / dc_data (resetless).
     - Read through a registered lookahead keyed on the EX ALU address, as r7s1 did:
       cand_hit_q / cand_data_q, reloaded only when EX/MEM advances, with same-word
       store-merge and load-fill bypasses.
     - Filled by bus loads.
     - Updated by every store at post time: merge on a cand hit or a full word,
       invalidate a partial-store miss.
     - ld_word = bus_free ? dmem_rdata : cand_data_q feeds the load extraction and
       MEM/WB.mem_rdata.
     - Coherence: this core is the only dmem master and every store updates the cache.
       The MMIO window is never cached.
   - Size: DC_IDX_W = 10 (1024 entries, index addr[11:2], tag addr[31:12]).
     - Size is free in the bench.
     - r4s1 measured 97.2% hits at 256 entries on 611 unique words.
     - Measure 8 vs 10 in cosim and keep the lower cycle count.

Why the netlist must fold exactly. Once io_dmemReady=1 is propagated:
  - sb_valid_q has D = 0 and reset 0, so opt_dff makes it constant 0.
  - bus_free = 1, mem_ready = 1, dmem_stall = 0, so hold_id = ex_div_busy, as today.
  - dmem_addr = EX/MEM.alu_result, exactly as today. This is critical: yosys absorbs
    those flops as the read-address register of the 4 DPX9B BSRAMs that implement the
    bench dmem. Any extra combinational term on dmem_addr breaks that inference.
  - ld_word = dmem_rdata, so cand_* / dc_* / sb payload are dead and get removed.

Acceptance, beyond the usual lint / cocotb / formal / cosim:
  (1) Synthesize core_bench_si with the eval's synth.tcl. The stat block must equal
      r7s0's exactly: 2839 cells; LUT1 204, LUT2 205, LUT3 1093, LUT4 914,
      MUX2_LUT5 367, ALU 386, RAM16SDP4 32, DPX9B 4, MULT36X36 1, DFF 49, DFFC 31,
      DFFE 263, DFFP 1, DFFR 566, DFFRE 358, DFFSE 1.
      If any count differs, find the surviving new logic and restructure it until it
      folds. r7s1's +5 FF / -5 LUT is exactly the residue that re-rolled P&R.
      - Check that no sb_/dc_/cand_ cell names remain in synth.json.
      - Keep existing net names on the ready=1 datapath where you can, so ABC9 and
        nextpnr see the same design.
  (2) Run nextpnr seeds 1/2/3. If the netlist is equivalent, expect 219.20 / 228.68 /
      209.07 MHz. Report whatever you get.

Expected cycles: D-side -184k (r7s1, same base cycle count) plus I-side -23k gives
about 3,199k (-6.1%), against a no-stall floor of 3,191,647.
Expected fitness: at the inherited 219.2 MHz median, 10 / 3.199M x 219.2e6 = ~685
(+6.5%). If the netlist still differs slightly and takes r4s1's ~3% haircut, it is
about +3%.
The change is orthogonal to the F/D Fmax limiters (BHT read, decode) and to the
load->branch speculation (r7s2), so it stacks with the other slots' work.

  derived localparams follow.

Re-apply r7s1's stall-only D-side pair.

New ports:

  lint_off UNUSEDSIGNAL), ex_adv (= !stall_ex_mem)
- output: mem_ready

1-entry posted store buffer:
- sb_valid_q <= !dmem_ready && (sb_valid_q || st), reset to 0.
- The payload regs capture while !sb_valid_q.
- dmem_* outputs select sb_* (ren = 0) while sb_valid_q, else today's expressions.
  Keep them free of dmem_ready so dmem_addr folds to in.alu_result (BSRAM
  address-register absorption in the bench).

Direct-mapped stall-only load cache:
- localparam DC_IDX_W = 10 (try 8; keep the lower cosim cycle count).
- dc_valid is reset; dc_tag and dc_data are resetless.
- Registered cand_hit_q/cand_data_q lookahead keyed on ex_addr, updated only when
  ex_adv, with same-word store-merge and load-fill bypasses.
- Fill on ld && bus_free && cacheable.
- On st_done: merge or allocate on cand hit or a full word, otherwise invalidate.
- Never cache addr[28] (MMIO).

Datapath:
- ld_word = bus_free ? dmem_rdata : cand_data_q feeds the load extraction and
  MEM/WB.mem_rdata.
- mem_ready = bus_free || (ld && cand_hit_q) || st_done.

Unchanged: the misalign trap (waits for bus_free, never posts or fills) and
hold_wb.

Update the header: stall-only, single-master coherence, folds away with ready=1.

- Rename input dmem_ready to mem_ready (the MEM op completes this cycle via the
  bus, a cache hit, or a store post).
- dmem_stall = !mem_ready && ex_mem_mem_op.

- It feeds only mem_stage's registered lookahead and is dead in the ready=1
  netlist.
- Nothing else in EX changes.

Wiring:
- io_dmemReady -> u_mem.dmem_ready
- u_ex.ex_addr -> u_mem.ex_addr
- !stall_ex_mem -> u_mem.ex_adv
- u_mem.mem_ready -> u_hazard.mem_ready, replacing io_dmemReady

Top-level IO and the nret=1 RVFI port set are unchanged. Update the header diagram
comment.

Port r7s1's test changes:
(a) Drive a POISON word on io_dmemRData on dready=0 cycles. A load that retires
    correctly on a refused cycle can then only have come from the cache.

    post.

title: Speculate load-dependent branches on the BHT and verify them in MEM, stacked on the LUT-RAM (r7s0) core with redirect taken off the ID/EX data cone
motivation:
The current best core (r7s0, 643.41 = 10 / 3,406,859 cycles x 219.2 MHz)
has the same cycle count as r5s0. So the r5s2/r7s2 trace breakdown of the
~485k excess cycles still applies:
  - load-use stalls: 203,959
      load -> BRANCH  135,320 (17 static sites; 0x484/0x490/0x548/0x550 ~28k each)
      load -> load     59,270
      load -> other     9,369
  - dmem random stalls: ~190k (memory category, not a predictor issue)
  - BRANCH mispredicts: 51,846 (1 bubble each)
  - JALR/ret: 13,735
The other predictor upgrades have low ceilings. On this trace, gshare or
gselect up to 1024 entries saves only ~10-12k cycles (0.35%), and a RAS
saves at most 13.7k (0.4%). By far the biggest predictor lever is the

r7s0 changes the timing picture in two ways:
(1) Load-use/redirect no longer drives the ~240-flop ID/EX CE. Flush now
    clears only 8 control flops, and hold_id = dmem_stall || div_busy
    folds to div_busy on the bench. The old CE risk is therefore mostly
    gone.
(2) At 4.56 ns, the limiters are short ~4.4-4.5 ns paths: div ITER, and
    EX/MEM.rd -> fwd select -> fwd mux -> div start.

NOP mux on out.instr -> decoder / imm_gen / alu_predecode -> the ~200-bit
ID/EX data half. r7s2's good build ended on ID/EX D inputs on every seed.

correctness. A bubble's data half is inert by construction, because every
side effect keys off the flush-cleared control bits. So this hypothesis

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Let a BRANCH that reads the rd of the LOAD directly ahead of it enter EX
without the load-use stall. EX sees a stale operand for it, so EX neither
redirects nor traps it. One stage later, MEM compares it against the
registered MEM/WB.read_data. A correctly predicted load-dependent branch
then costs 0 cycles instead of 1. A mispredicted one costs 2 bubbles, the
same as today's 1 stall + 1 redirect bubble. No case gets slower.

Mechanism (the r5s2/r7s2 design, which passed formal and cosim twice):
1. hazard_unit: split the match into ld_rs1 / ld_rs2 against a registered
   id_ex_ld_nz (= mem_read && rd != 0, precomputed in ID).
   load_use_hazard = (ld_rs1 || ld_rs2) && !if_id_is_branch.
   late_rs1 = ld_rs1 && if_id_is_branch, and likewise late_rs2.
   if_id_is_branch is IF's existing predecode pd_br. It is computed in
   parallel with the 5-bit rd compares, so the final stall gate stays at
   4 inputs {ld_nz, eq1, eq2, pd_br}. late_rs1/late_rs2 feed only
   ID/EX control-half D inputs.
2. id_stage: late_rs1, late_rs2 and ld_nz go into the ID/EX control half
   (cleared on reset || flush, captured when !hold).
3. ex_stage: late = late_rs1 || late_rs2 gates the EX redirect and
   misalign_branch. New input kill (= mem_redirect) makes the EX slot
   wrong-path. EX/MEM then captures valid=0, reg_write/mem_read/mem_write/
   is_branch/is_jump = 0 and late flags = 0. A wrong-path STORE must never
   reach MEM, because dmem_wen is combinational from EX/MEM. EX/MEM also
   carries tgt_misalign (branch_target[1:0] != 0), pred_taken,
   alt_target, bht_ctr, the late flags, and a 2-bit bht_upd. bht_upd is
   the EX-resolved counter; its compare only selects between inc/dec
   values precomputed from ID/EX flops. Per the r7s2 lesson, do NOT add a
   flop of the raw 1-bit EX branch_cond. That build fell to 113-132 MHz.
4. mem_stage verify: late = in.valid && (late_rs1 || late_rs2).
   op1 = late_rs1 ? MEM/WB.read_data : in.rs1_val, and likewise op2.
   Every source here is a register. A six-way compare gives cond_late,
   and taken_late = cond_late && !tgt_misalign.
   replay = !MEM/WB.ctrl.reg_write (the misaligned-load trap left rd
   unwritten).
   mem_redirect = late && (replay || (taken_late ^ pred_taken)), with
   target = replay ? pc : alt_target.
   MEM/WB gets the corrected rs1_val/rs2_val (RVFI) and pc_next, is_illegal
   |= cond_late && tgt_misalign, and valid = 0 on replay. The load and the
   branch move in lockstep: a late branch is never a mem op, so it sits in
   EX/MEM for exactly one cycle, and in that cycle MEM/WB is exactly the
   load.
5. The BHT write port moves from EX to MEM for every branch. It is
   registered and lands the next cycle. For a late branch, cond_late
   selects inc/dec of the carried bht_ctr; otherwise bht_upd is used.
   Only correct-path branches reach MEM, which also removes wrong-path and
   held-EX repeat writes. Trace replay shows identical mispredict counts.
6. core.sv: redirect = mem_redirect || (ex_redirect && !late), written as
   one expression so ABC can merge it into the existing gate. MEM is
   older and wins. Target = (is_jalr && !mem_redirect) ? jalr_sum :
   (mem_redirect ? mem_target : alt_target). This keeps the late-arriving
   jalr_sum at one mux level; the inner mux and its select come only from
   registers.

New for r7s0, to keep the 219 MHz netlist:
(a) Redirect off the ID/EX data-half cone. Feed id_stage's decoder,
    imm_gen, alu_predecode and d_next.instr from the raw fetched word
    (instr_word, live or replayed), not from the kill-muxed out.instr.
    Also feed the hazard unit's if_id_rs1/rs2/is_branch from the raw word.
    Apply kill (flush_if = redirect || imem_stall) only to the control
    half: valid, pred_taken, reg_write, mem_read, mem_write, is_branch,
    is_jump, is_div, late_rs1/2 and ld_nz, e.g. by ANDing their D with
    in.valid. That is one short gate next to the existing flush clear.
    This is safe on r7s0:
      - A bubble's data half is already inert.
      - During redirect, flush_id is already 1, and a spurious raw-word
        load-use only raises stall_if, which pc_d's redirect priority
        overrides.
      - During imem_stall, the control half is cleared through the
        in.valid gate. This does NOT go through flush_id, whose priority
        over hold would wipe a busy DIV.
    The r3s2 lesson against dropping redirect from the NOP mux applied
    only when load-use drove the whole ID/EX CE, which r7s0 removed.
    imem_stall folds to 0 on the bench, so there the control-half gate
    is just !redirect. RVFI is unchanged, because it keys off valid.
(b) Divide kill without putting the late compare on the div start
    enable. Keep start = in.valid && is_div, straight from registers.
    Instead, div_unit returns to IDLE on any non-IDLE cycle where start
    is low. A real divide holds start high from launch until ack, because
    ID/EX is held by div_busy/dmem_stall. So the only way start drops
    mid-divide is a MEM-redirect flush of a wrong-path DIV in EX. A
    wrong-path DIV that started on the kill edge is then dropped the next
    cycle, before a later real DIV could pick up its result.

Expected cycles: 3,406,859 -> ~3,278,600 (-3.77%). The model and two
prototypes agreed to within 175 cycles. That is +3.9% fitness at equal
Fmax. With (a), the redirect net loses its largest fan-out cone, so Fmax
should hold at ~219 MHz or rise. Without (a), expect a 0-4% Fmax haircut.
Area: ~+300 LUT4 and ~+60 FF (3,080 -> ~3,400 LUT4, far under 10k).
None of this touches the imem/dmem ready paths, so the replay store still
constant-folds on the bench. One RVFI don't-care: mem_rdata may differ on
non-memory retirements (rmask = 0). Neither run_cosim.py nor
riscv-formal checks it.

Validation: cosim --bench --istall --dstall must reach 3,278,562 +/- a
few hundred cycles with CRCs and "Correct operation validated". The
architectural RVFI stream (cycle field dropped) must be byte-identical to
r7s0's on CoreMark and selftest. Run 3-seed P&R and report the worst
seed. If any seed ends on mem_redirect -> pc_d or -> EX/MEM kill at
< 210 MHz, check that the redirect expression was merged as in step 6.

lesson: - 2026-09-26 hyp-20260926-003-r9s2 (regression, -5.02%): The third build of the late load->branch MEM verify, now on r7s0 with redirect taken off the decode -> ID/EX data cone (raw word into decode, kill applied only to the control half through a fetched/valid gate), again landed its exact cycles (3,406,859->3,278,562, -3.77%, formal 53/53) but cost 8.6% Fmax (219.2->200.4 MHz, seeds 201.4/187.7/200.4, +288 LUT4), because every seed now ends on the untouched ID/EX alu_ctl.sub -> adder carry chain -> SLT carry chain -> 3-LUT4 result/div-result merge -> EX/MEM.alu_result path (4.01 ns of logic, against 2.29 ns on r7s0's BHT->ID/EX limiter), which ABC9 also mapped deeper in a raw-word-decode-only ablation (seeds 216/184/223), while restoring the IF NOP mux instead gave 143-154 MHz on a fwd -> ALU -> pred_taken compare -> PC path; so any MEM-side redirect needs redirect decoupled from decode, but at ~4.5 ns a -3.8% cycle win is smaller than the re-roll exposure of the ALU->EX/MEM result merge, so shorten that path first (pre-select or register the SLT/div-result terms) before re-applying the late branch.

title: Take the divider off every critical path: plain operand latch at start + two-phase registered restoring step (div_unit.sv only, cycle-neutral)
motivation:
I re-ran synth + 3-seed P&R on the current core (r9s1) locally and got the
logged seeds exactly (240.44 / 222.07 / 214.55 MHz), so the netlist below
is the scored one. On all three seeds the critical path ends inside
div_unit, although CoreMark retires no divides in the timed bracket:

  - seed 2 (222.07 MHz, 4.50 ns) and seed 3 (214.55 MHz, 4.66 ns):
    EX/MEM.rd -> forward_unit compare (2 LUT4) -> fwd mux -> rs1[31] ->
    div_unit.neg_q.D. This is the IDLE-arm start capture
    (neg_q <= !is_unsigned && a[31]). rq_q / dvs_q / a_q / b_q / dneg_q
    also load straight from the fwd-mux outputs on that edge. The path has
    1.95 ns of logic and 2.6-2.7 ns of routing, because the div flops sit
    far from the forwarding network and every rs1/rs2 bit fans out to
    2 extra div loads.
  - seed 1 (240.44 MHz, 4.16 ns): the ITER step. rq_q[31] -> 34-bit
    trial-subtract carry chain -> `take` fans out (0.74 ns routing) to
    64 rem_q/rq_q muxes -> rem_q.D.

So the whole scored median is a tax paid for an op the benchmark never
executes in the timed region, and the lesson from r1s1 applies again one
level down. A slower divider is free. I measured the prototype below
under cosim --istall --dstall: 3,194,453 bracketed cycles, 46 fewer than
the current 3,194,499 because the stall stream shifts slightly. No
divides are in the bracket.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Change only rtl/div_unit.sv, in two ways, so that no divider path
approaches the clock period:

(1) Operand latch only on the start edge. IDLE+start now does only
    a_q <= a, b_q <= b, is_rem_q, is_uns_q, a plain enabled copy of the
    fwd-mux outputs with no logic after them. A new ST_SIGN state (3'd5)
    then loads rq_q <= a_q, dvs_q <= b_q, neg_q / dneg_q from
    a_q[31] / b_q[31] and sel_rem_q <= 0, and goes to PREP. PREP, FIXUP,
    DONE and the corner-case handling are unchanged. Under
    RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, start still goes straight to PREP, which already
    computed alt_result from a_q / b_q, so the formal latency stays at
    2 cycles and the formal-visible behaviour is unchanged.
(2) Two-phase ITER. iter_hi_q toggles every ITER cycle. The compare phase
    registers take_q <= take and step_diff_q <= diff[31:0], so the carry
    chain ends in flops. The apply phase does the old step from those
    flops: rem_q <= take_q ? step_diff_q : trial, rq_q shift-in take_q,
    cnt_q--, the sel_rem_q / neg_q fold, and exit to FIXUP at cnt 0.
    rem_q and rq_q don't change during the compare phase, so trial is
    the same in both phases. Divide latency goes from 34 to 67 cycles.

Measured locally with the exact text given under changes (yosys
synth_gowin + nextpnr-himbaechel via fpga/scripts, core_bench_si):
  - seeds 1/2/3 = 259.27 / 274.65 / 274.65 MHz. The median is 274.65,
    against 222.07 now.
  - seeds 4-8 = 274.65 / 274.65 / 274.65 / 259.54 / 239.98. This is the
    netlist's typical result, not luck on seeds 1-3.
  - No seed ends in div_unit any more. On the 274.65 seeds the limit is
    the 64-bit rvfi_order_q +1 carry chain: 3.64 ns, 3.47 ns of it logic,
    a fixed ceiling. Seed 1 ends on imem word -> decode ->
    ID/EX reg_write_q (3.86 ns).
  - Cells: LUT4 911, LUT3 1091, LUT2 205, LUT1 210, MUX2_LUT5 367,
    ALU 386, DFFRE 392 (+34 over today: take_q, step_diff_q, iter_hi_q),
    DFFR 566.
  - Fitness = 274.65e6 * 10 / 3,194,453 = 859.8 iter/s, +23.7% over 695.16.

Re-roll caveat (per the r9s1 lesson, and measured here). The same logic
with three identifiers spelled differently (ph_q / ST_LOAD / diff_q
instead of iter_hi_q / ST_SIGN / step_diff_q) mapped the ID decode cone
differently in ABC9 and gave 251.26 / 242.31 / 224.97. Its 8-seed mean
was 241.9 MHz, against 227.3 for the current core over the same 8 seeds.
So the durable gain is about +6-9% and the exact text is worth about
+24%. Comments, line numbers and the RTL path do NOT change the netlist.
I verified that the fully commented final file gives the identical cell
stats and seeds as the bare prototype, and that the current RTL copied to

lesson: - 2026-09-26 hyp-20260926-001-r10s0 (improvement, +23.68%): After r1s1 made DIV/REM multi-cycle, div_unit still ended the critical path on every seed, even though CoreMark retires no divides in the timed bracket: the IDLE start capture (fwd mux -> rs1[31] -> neg_q, 4.5-4.66 ns, mostly routing to the far-placed div flops) and the ITER step (34-bit trial-subtract -> `take` fanned out to 64 rem/rq muxes). Two changes removed it: the start edge became a plain enabled a_q/b_q copy, with the signs and rq/dvs loads moved to a new ST_SIGN state, and each restoring step was split into a compare phase that registers take/diff[31:0] and an apply phase. Latency went 34->67 cycles, cycles barely moved (3,194,499->3,194,453), the median rose 222.07->274.65 MHz and the score matched it, and the new fixed ceiling is the 64-bit rvfi_order_q +1 carry chain (3.64 ns, 3.47 ns of it logic). Only about +6-9% of the gain is durable: the same logic with three identifiers renamed re-rolled ABC9's ID-decode mapping to 251/242/225 MHz (8-seed mean 241.9 vs 227.3). So for any unit the timed loop never exercises, register every path into and inside it (extra latency is free there), treat identifier renames as P&R re-rolls, and expect a split rvfi_order_q or a reg_write-from-opcode ID/EX change to re-roll or lengthen the ID/EX cone, as both did here.

motivation:

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the single 64-bit increment with two 32-bit halves: the low half
increments on every retirement, and the high half increments one cycle
later from a registered "low half wrapped" flag, while the RVFI output
adds the pending carry back combinationally-free by construction (the

title: Resolve every conditional BRANCH in MEM from registered operands (no load->branch stall, no EX branch comparator)
motivation:
The current core runs 3,194,453 bracketed cycles for about 2.94M retirements.
Bus stalls are used up (r9s1 got within 3k of the no-stall floor). Per the
RVFI breakdowns logged in r5s2/r7s2/r9s2, the remaining bubbles are:
  load-use                 ~204k  (load -> BRANCH 135.3k at 17 static sites,
                                   load -> load 59.3k, load -> other 9.4k)
  BRANCH mispredicts        51.8k (1 bubble each)
  JALR (all returns)        13.7k
The rest of the predictor space is small. gshare/gselect up to 1024 entries
saves 10-12k cycles and a RAS saves 13.7k, each about 0.4%. The load -> BRANCH
stall is the only predictor lever over 1%. The BHT already predicts all of
those branches at fetch, so the branch needs the loaded value only to *verify*
the prediction.

That verify has been built three times (r5s2, r7s2, r9s2), always as a HYBRID:
branches resolve in EX, and only the load-dependent ones move to MEM. Each time
the cycles landed exactly (-3.77%). Each time Fmax was the problem, because the
hybrid keeps the long EX cone
  forward_unit rd compare -> 3:1 fwd mux -> 32-bit compare -> branch_op
  select -> redirect -> {pc_d, IF NOP mux -> decode -> ID/EX, flush_id}
and adds a second MEM redirect source plus a priority mux on top of it. The
design is at 274.65 MHz (3.64 ns) and its fixed ceiling is the rvfi_order_q
carry chain, so there is no slack to spend on more redirect logic.

This proposal is a different trade. Move ALL conditional-branch resolution to
MEM and compute it only from flops: EX/MEM.rs1_val/rs2_val (already
registered post-forward values), or the MEM/WB load result through a 2:1 mux
whose select is a flop. EX then has no branch comparator and no branch
redirect. Its only redirect is JALR, whose redirect bit is flop + fwd mux +
2-bit add (the misalign bit).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Cycle model, from the logged trace numbers:
  - load -> BRANCH stalls removed:                    -135.3k
  - each BRANCH mispredict costs 2 bubbles, not 1:    +51.8k
  - BHT written 1 cycle later (update lag):           +~1-3k
  net about -82k => ~3.11M cycles (-2.6%). JALR stays in EX at 1 bubble.
Fmax: this deletes the fwd-mux -> comparator -> redirect cone from EX and the
comparator's fan-in on the rs1/rs2 fwd-mux nets that also feed the ALU. It
replaces them with a MEM-stage compare whose inputs are flops, or a flop-
selected 2:1 mux of flops. The redirect net therefore arrives about two LUT
levels earlier at pc_d, at the IF NOP mux and at the ID/EX control-half
clear. Budget a +-3-6% ABC9/P&R re-roll as usual. The implementer should
3-seed P&R before and after, and report the worst paths.

Design (single-issue, nret=1, RVFI contract unchanged):

1. Hazard (hazard_unit.sv, if_stage.sv, core.sv): a conditional branch in ID is
   exempt from load-use. load_use = ld_nz && (rd==rs1 || rd==rs2) && !id_is_br.
   id_is_br is IF's existing pd_br for the word going to ID, exported on
   if_id_t, e.g. out.is_br = pd_br && !kill. Keep the load-use gate narrow,
   following the r7s2 lesson: register ld_nz = mem_read && rd!=0 in ID/EX
   (control half) if it is not already cheap, and check with a timing report
   that the load-use -> ID/EX CE/clear path does not get longer. JALR,
   stores and every other consumer keep today's load-use stall.

2. forward_unit / EX/MEM: forward from EX/MEM only when it is NOT a load. Add a
   registered EX/MEM flop fwd_en = ctrl_with_trap.reg_write && !mem_read and
   feed it to forward_unit in place of ex_mem reg_write, so the compare LUTs
   keep the same input count. Today this changes nothing, because a
   non-branch consumer of a load one ahead is always stalled. It makes the
   value a late branch captures in EX (EX/MEM.rs?_val) the correct
   architectural value to fall back on if the load does not write rd
   (misaligned-load trap): MEM/WB forward, or the ID/EX regfile value.

3. EX (ex_stage.sv): remove branch_cond / branch_taken / misalign_branch and
   the branch term from redirect. redirect_ex = is_jump(ctrl half) && is_jalr
   && !misalign_jump. JAL is always predicted taken, and a misaligned JAL is
   never predicted and traps, so JAL never redirects, as today. Register into
   EX/MEM, all from flops or short EX logic, never from a compare:
     late_rs1/late_rs2 = ex_mem.mem_read && ex_mem.reg_write && ex_mem.rd!=0
                         && ex_mem.rd == in.rs1_addr/rs2_addr
     pred_taken, alt_target, branch_op (already in ctrl), branch_target
     (already there), br_tgt_mis = branch_target[1]
     bht_inc / bht_dec (2 bits each, precomputed from in.bht_ctr; this is the
     r7s2 lesson: register values the late compare only SELECTS between,
     never a raw compare bit)
   pc_next for a branch is registered as pc+4. MEM fixes it up when taken.
   Kill on MEM redirect: when mem_redirect fires, EX/MEM captures a bubble.
   Clear valid and the side-effect ctrl bits (reg_write, mem_read,
   mem_write, is_branch, is_jump, fwd_en) with a sync clear of those few flops
   only. Do not fan it into the whole EX/MEM enable. The wrong-path
   instruction in EX may be a load/store, a JALR (its redirect_ex is
   overridden, MEM is older) or a DIV (see 5).

4. MEM (mem_stage.sv, or a small branch block beside it in core.sv):
     rs1_m = (late_rs1_q && mem_wb.ctrl.reg_write) ? mem_wb.read_data : in.rs1_val
     rs2_m likewise (one LUT4 per bit: 2 flop selects, 2 flop data)
     cond  = branch_op compare of rs1_m, rs2_m (same 6-way compare as EX today)
     taken = in.valid && in.ctrl.is_branch && cond && !in.br_tgt_mis
     mem_redirect   = in.valid && in.ctrl.is_branch && (taken ^ in.pred_taken)
     mem_target     = in.alt_target
     trap: is_illegal |= is_branch && cond && br_tgt_mis
     MEM/WB.pc_next = taken ? in.branch_target : in.pc_next
     MEM/WB.rs1_val/rs2_val = rs1_m/rs2_m, so RVFI reports the loaded value.
   A branch has no memory op, so it never sits in MEM for more than one cycle,
   and MEM/WB holds the load (valid, data intact) for that cycle.
   BHT write (bht_we/widx/wdata into IF) moves here, registered one cycle
   later as today: we_q <= in.valid && is_branch, widx_q <= in.pc[7:2],
   wdata_q <= cond ? in.bht_inc : in.bht_dec.

5. core.sv redirect merge: redirect = mem_redirect || redirect_ex. Target =
   mem_redirect ? mem_target (flop) : jalr_target. Write it as one expression
   so the late jalr_sum stays at one mux level. mem_redirect also drives
   hazard flush_if/flush_id exactly as redirect does today, and the new
   EX/MEM kill. It overrides stall in pc_d as today. It may now coincide with
   ex_div_busy (hold_id): the control-half clear already wins over hold in
   id_stage, so fix the comment that says the two are never high together.
   div_unit: a wrong-path DIV in EX may have started on the redirect edge. Make
   the unit return to IDLE on any non-IDLE, non-DONE cycle where start is low
   (the r9s2 scheme). A real divide holds start (= valid && is_div from
   registers) high from launch to ack, so only a killed divide ever drops it.
   This is register-only. Do NOT gate start with mem_redirect. Keep the
   ALTOPS arm consistent.

6. Keep kill = flush || redirect on the IF NOP/valid mux, as the r3s2 lesson
   requires. redirect is now earlier-arriving, which is the point.
   pred_taken/bht_ctr/alt_target still travel IF -> ID/EX -> EX/MEM.

Correctness watch-points for formal/cosim:
  - late branch after a misaligned (trapping) load: handled by 2 (fallback
    value) and by the mem_wb.ctrl.reg_write term in 4.
  - two consecutive branches: the younger is in EX when the older redirects
    from MEM, and it is killed (bubble) by 3.
  - branch directly after a load that dmem-stalls: the branch waits in ID/EX
    (hold) and enters EX/MEM on the edge the load enters MEM/WB, so the late
    flag and read_data line up. Test it under --istall --dstall.
  - rvfi_order / valid: killed EX/MEM entries have valid=0.

Validation to run: cocotb (all suites), formal (checks_si), CoreMark cosim
--istall --dstall. Expect ~3.11M cycles and RVFI byte-identical except for
timing. Also 3-seed P&R with the worst 5 paths. If a seed ends on the MEM
compare -> redirect -> pc_d/ID/EX path, register-balance it. For example,
precompute rs1_m == rs2_m pieces or the LT carry from flops. Do not
reintroduce an EX compare.

title: Late branch unit: resolve load-dependent BRANCHes in MEM from registered operands, redirect one cycle later from a flop (WB-stage redirect port)
motivation:
Replaying the RVFI trace of the current core's cycle profile (2,922,015
retired instructions in 3,194,453 cycles, so ~272k bubbles) splits the
bubbles into 135,320 load->branch stalls, 59,270 load->load address
stalls, 51,846 BRANCH mispredicts, 13,735 JALRs, ~9k load->ALU and ~0.4k
load->store-data. Load->branch is the largest single item (4.2% of all
cycles). Most of it comes from CoreMark's two inlined core_list_find
loops (0x480-0x490 and 0x540-0x550): 5 instructions each, where
`lw a5,0(a5); beqz a5` and `lh/lbu x,..; bne/beq x,..` each stall one
cycle every iteration (~57k iterations in total).

Moving the branch compare later has been tried four times. Each time the
cycle count came out as modeled, and each time Fmax dropped. r9s2 and
r11s2 lost Fmax through ABC9 re-mapping the ALU->EX/MEM adder/SLT merge,
which r12s1 then hardened into a single two-operand 34-bit chain. The
earlier MEM-redirect builds also put a same-cycle
"late compare -> redirect -> pc_d / IF kill / ID/EX control clear" cone
in front of the PC and the ID/EX register. On today's 3.3-3.5 ns fabric
(current worst paths: EX/MEM.instr -> illegal decode -> MEM/WB trap, and
imem -> decode -> ID/EX reg_write_q) that cone would become the new
limiter.

The structural fix is to avoid that cone entirely. Late branches
mispredict rarely: only 7,198 of the 135,320 load-dependent branches
mispredict under the 64-entry bimodal BHT. So the MEM compare can end
in a flop, and the redirect can fire a cycle later. The cost is 1 extra
bubble on ~7.2k events (7.2k cycles). The gain is that every redirect
and kill consumer sees a flop, not a compare.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a "late branch" path: a conditional BRANCH that reads the rd of the
LOAD directly ahead of it skips the load-use stall. The branch is
checked in MEM against the load's registered MEM/WB.read_data, and a
mispredict is registered and redirected from the following cycle (the
branch is then in WB).

1. ID (hazard_unit + id_stage). Today load_use_hazard is
   ld && rd!=0 && (rd==rs1 || rd==rs2). It becomes
   ld_nz_q && (m1 || m2) && !if_br, where:
     - ld_nz_q = mem_read && rd!=0, registered in ID/EX (r7s2's trick
       to keep the final gate 4-input);
     - if_br is IF's existing predecode pd_br (valid-funct3 BRANCH),
       exported on if_id_t.
   When ld_nz_q && (m1 || m2) && if_br, ID/EX captures the branch as
   "late":
     - Control half: late_q = 1, late_rs1_q = m1, late_rs2_q = m2.
       is_branch_q and pred_taken_q are captured as 0, so EX treats it
       as an inert non-redirecting op: no EX redirect, no EX BHT write,
       no EX misalign trap from the stale compare.
     - The real fetch-time prediction travels in the data half
       (data_q.pred_taken, bht_ctr, alt_target, imm[1]).

2. EX. Pass the late fields through into EX/MEM: late, late_rs1,
   late_rs2, late_pred, bht_ctr, alt_target, branch_op, and the
   misaligned-target flag imm[1]. No new logic sits on the ALU ->
   EX/MEM path. The non-load operand is already forwarded correctly in
   EX: its rs does not match EX/MEM.rd. It lands in EX/MEM.rs?_val as
   today.

3. MEM, the late branch unit. The operands come only from flops:
     - a = late_rs1 ? MEM/WB.read_data : EX/MEM.rs1_val
     - b = late_rs2 ? MEM/WB.read_data : EX/MEM.rs2_val
   The load is guaranteed to sit in MEM/WB at that moment. Both
   instructions leave ID/EX -> EX/MEM -> MEM/WB on the same hold
   edges, and hold_mem_wb only fires for a mem op in EX/MEM, which a
   branch is not.
   A six-way compare over (a, b) gives cond. From cond, register:
     - late_mis_q = valid && late && !late_kill
                    && ((cond && !imm1) != late_pred)
       (IF never predicts a misaligned target, so a taken + misaligned
       late branch traps and falls through: no mispredict.)
     - into MEM/WB, 1-bit late_taken / late_trap flags. RVFI pc_wdata
       (= branch_target when taken) and rvfi_trap are fixed up at the
       core.sv RVFI outputs from these registered bits. The compare
       never drives a 32-bit pc_next mux or the already-critical
       EX/MEM.instr -> illegal-decode -> MEM/WB.is_illegal flop.
     - MEM/WB.rs?_val <= late_rs? ? MEM/WB.read_data : rs?_val, so
       RVFI rs?_rdata is exact.
     - A 2-bit BHT update: cond selects between inc/dec counters
       precomputed from the carried bht_ctr (r7s2's lesson: register a
       value the compare selects, never the raw compare bit).
   The MEM BHT write is registered and has priority over EX's
   registered write on the shared port. A dropped EX write is only a
   lost hint.

4. WB-stage redirect, one cycle later, from flops only:
     - late_kill = late_mis_q
     - late_tgt_q = registered alt_target, the path IF did not take
   Fold late_kill into the existing redirect net:
     - redirect = (actual ^ pred_taken) | late_kill. This is a spare
       LUT input, so it adds no level.
     - redirect_target = late_kill ? late_tgt_q
                                   : (is_jalr ? jalr : alt_target).
       The select is a flop, and it is off the compare path.
   So flush_if, flush_id, the IF NOP/valid kill and pc_d need no new
   logic. late_kill also clears, as flop-driven sync clears:
     - EX/MEM capture: valid, reg_write, mem_read, mem_write, is_branch,
       late;
     - MEM/WB capture of the MEM-stage instruction: valid and reg_write,
       so a killed writer can never be forwarded by forward_unit, which
       keys on reg_write;
     - the MEM-stage store: dmem_wen, st_done / store-buffer post, cache
       update and ex_mem_mem_op into dmem_stall;
     - div_unit: a new kill input returns it to IDLE, so an orphaned
       wrong-path divide can never hand its result to a later DIV.
   In the io_dmemReady=1 bench the new store gating is one AND from a
   flop on dmem_wen.

Expected: CoreMark cycles 3,194,453 -> ~3,073,529 (-3.79%, from the
trace model with the 3-bubble registered redirect; a same-cycle MEM
redirect would reach 3,066,331, only 7.2k better). RVFI stays
byte-identical except for cycle stamps.

Fmax: the new logic is flop -> mux -> compare -> flop in MEM, plus
flop-driven clears. The compare is similar in depth to today's EX
compare, but its operands come from flops instead of the forward mux,
and it ends in ~4 flops with no 32-bit fanout.
The two risks:

    !if_br. Mitigation: registered ld_nz, and pd_br already computed
    in IF in parallel with the rs compares;
  - the usual ±3-6% P&R re-roll of any non-parameter edit.
Project from the worst seed. Accept only if the 3-seed median stays
>= ~280 MHz. If a seed ends on the new hazard term, try computing
if_br from instr_word[6:2] only (the valid-funct3 check is not needed
for the stall decision: a reserved-funct3 BRANCH traps anyway, and a
"late" flag on it only skips a stall).

title: Speculate load-dependent branches on the BHT and verify them in MEM, on the r12s1 core (with RVFI-trap and redirect timing guards)
motivation:
I measured the current best core (r12s1: 894.39 = 10 / 3,194,453 cycles x 285.71 MHz)
with the eval's own tools.

Cycles. Cosim with NRET=1, --istall --dstall, full RVFI trace, bracketed by the
0x10000100 / 0x10000104 markers: 2,922,017 retirements in 3,194,453 cycles, so
272,437 bubbles. Classified from the trace:
  load -> BRANCH (load-use stall)   135,322   (49.7%)
  load -> load   (load-use stall)    59,353
  BRANCH mispredict (1 bubble)       51,852
  JALR (always redirected)           13,742
  load -> ALU/store                   9,372
  bus stalls (unhidden)               2,796
My trace model of the 64-entry bimodal BHT predicts 51,846 mispredicts, against
51,852 in the trace, so the replay is accurate.

Other predictor options have low ceilings on this trace:
- Bimodal 256 / 1024: 44,266 / 39,617 mispredicts, at most 7.6k-12k cycles (0.2-0.4%).
  It would also add a 16:1 read mux on the fetch BHT -> pred_raw -> pc_d path.
- gshare 64..1024 with h = 2..10: 38k-69k mispredicts, no better than bimodal-1024.
- A RAS for JALR: at most 13.7k cycles (0.43%), plus a new pc_d source.
- BHT update lag: visible at retire -1/0/+1/+2 all give exactly 51,846, so moving
  the BHT write one stage later costs nothing.

The one large predictor lever is the 135,320 load -> BRANCH stalls: 17 static sites,
the top four (0x484, 0x490, 0x548, 0x550) at ~28k each. The fetch-time BHT already
predicts every one of these branches, and gets 128,122 (94.7%) right. The branch
needs the loaded value only to verify the prediction, not to steer fetch.

History of this idea:
- r5s2 and r7s2: landed the exact modelled cycles (-128,297) and beat their base
  cores (+8.8% and +12.7%). Each lost the round to a sibling.
- r9s2 and r11s2: lost Fmax, because the untouched ID/EX alu_ctl.sub ->
  three-addend adder -> SLT -> result merge -> EX/MEM.alu_result path re-mapped.
- r12s1: fixed that adder (a single 34-bit two-operand chain with sub as the
  carry-in, plus a one-hot alu_ctl decoded straight from the instruction bits).
  LESSONS.md says the load->branch verify "can now be retried on this core with
  3-seed P&R".

Current timing. I re-ran P&R on the r12s1 netlist and reproduced 299.67 / 285.47 /
285.71 MHz exactly.
- Seeds 1 and 3 end on EX/MEM.instr -> full decoder is_illegal -> OR ->
  MEM/WB.ctrl.is_illegal (rvfi_trap). That is 3.34 / 3.50 ns, 4 LUT levels plus a
  MUX2_LUT6, and it feeds RVFI only.
- Seed 2 ends on imem_data -> decoder -> ID/EX reg_write_q.D (3.50 ns).
None of the three ends on the branch compare or redirect cone. The new MEM verify
logic lands in the same MEM-stage region as the rvfi_trap path, so this hypothesis
also takes the full illegal-decode off that path, as a guard against re-roll.

51,852 in the trace, so the replay is accurate.

Other predictor options have low ceilings on this trace:
- Bimodal 256 / 1024: 44,266 / 39,617 mispredicts, at most 7.6k-12k cycles (0.2-0.4%).
  It would also add a 16:1 read mux on the fetch BHT -> pred_raw -> pc_d path.
- gshare 64..1024 with h = 2..10: 38k-69k mispredicts, no better than bimodal-1024.
- A RAS for JALR: at most 13.7k cycles (0.43%), plus a new pc_d source.
- BHT update lag: visible at retire -1/0/+1/+2 all give exactly 51,846, so moving
  the BHT write one stage later costs nothing.

The one large predictor lever is the 135,320 load -> BRANCH stalls: 17 static sites,
the top four (0x484, 0x490, 0x548, 0x550) at ~28k each. The fetch-time BHT already
predicts every one of these branches, and gets 128,122 (94.7%) right. The branch
needs the loaded value only to verify the prediction, not to steer fetch.

History of this idea:
- r5s2 and r7s2: landed the exact modelled cycles (-128,297) and beat their base
  cores (+8.8% and +12.7%). Each lost the round to a sibling.
- r9s2 and r11s2: lost Fmax, because the untouched ID/EX alu_ctl.sub ->
  three-addend adder -> SLT -> result merge -> EX/MEM.alu_result path re-mapped.

  carry-in, plus a one-hot alu_ctl decoded straight from the instruction bits).

  3-seed P&R".

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Let a conditional BRANCH that reads the rd of the LOAD directly ahead of it enter
EX without the load-use stall. Its EX compare sees a stale operand, so EX neither
redirects on it nor writes the BHT for it. One stage later, in MEM, the branch is
compared against the registered MEM/WB.read_data. The load and the branch move in
lockstep:
- ID/EX captures only when EX/MEM also advances (hold_id = dmem_stall || div_busy,
  and a divide is never a load).
- EX/MEM never holds with a branch in it.
So MEM/WB is always exactly that load when the branch is in MEM.

Cost per case:
- Correctly predicted load-dependent branch: 0 bubbles (today 1).
- Mispredicted one: 2 bubbles (IF slot and EX slot killed), the same as today's
  1 stall + 1 redirect.
No case gets slower. Model: -128,122 cycles (3,194,453 -> ~3,066,331, -4.01%), so
+4.2% fitness at equal Fmax.

Mechanism (the r5s2/r7s2 design, adapted to the r12s1 RTL):
1. Eligibility (IF predecode). late_ok = pd_br && !pimm[1]. That is a valid-funct3
   BRANCH whose target can never be misaligned; IF already refuses to predict
   imm[1] targets. So a late branch can never raise the EX or MEM misalign trap,
   and MEM never needs a trap term for it. The killed-IF case needs no qualifier:
   the rs1/rs2 matches use if_id_w.instr, which is already the NOP on kill.
2. hazard_unit.
   - Add ld_nz = ctrl.mem_read && rd != 0, precomputed in ID and held in the ID/EX
     control half (cleared on reset/flush). It replaces id_ex_mem_read and the
     5-bit rd != 0 check, so the final stall gate stays at 4 inputs:
     {ld_nz, eq_rs1, eq_rs2, late_ok}.
   - load_use_hazard = ld_nz && (eq_rs1 || eq_rs2) && !late_ok.
   - late_rs1 = ld_nz && eq_rs1 && late_ok, and likewise late_rs2. These are
     data-only outputs into the ID/EX control half's D inputs, never onto a
     CE / reset.
3. id_stage: the control half gains late_rs1 and late_rs2, cleared on
   reset || flush like the other side-effect bits.
4. ex_stage.
   - late = in.late_rs1 || in.late_rs2.
   - ex_redirect = (actual_taken ^ pred_taken) && !late.
   - New input kill (= mem_redirect) makes EX's slot wrong-path. EX/MEM captures
     valid, ctrl.reg_write, mem_read, mem_write, is_branch, is_jump and late_rs*
     as 0; the data half is unchanged. A wrong-path STORE must never reach
     EX/MEM.mem_write, because dmem_wen is combinational from it.
   - The divide start is not gated by kill, since the div flops are far-placed.
     Instead ex_stage registers abort_q <= kill && div_req, and div_unit gains an
     abort input that forces state_q to ST_IDLE. A killed divide can only be on its
     first EX cycle, so the unit is in SIGN (or PREP under ALTOPS) and nothing
     else is lost.
   - The BHT write leaves EX. EX/MEM gains:
     - bht_upd[1:0] <= branch_cond ? ctr_inc : ctr_dec. This is the exact cone
       of today's bht_wdata_q. Per r7s2, do not register the raw 1-bit
       branch_cond.
     - bht_ctr[1:0], pred_taken, alt_target[31:0], late_rs1, late_rs2.
5. mem_stage verify.
   - late = in.valid && (in.late_rs1 || in.late_rs2).
   - op1 = in.late_rs1 ? reg_q.read_data : in.rs1_val, and likewise op2.
     reg_q is this module's own MEM/WB register; hold_wb keeps it alive.
   - A six-way compare on in.ctrl.branch_op gives cond_late. Every operand is a
     flop, so this is shorter than EX's forward-select -> 3:1 mux -> compare cone.
   - replay = !reg_q.ctrl.reg_write: a misaligned load trapped and did not write
     rd, so re-fetch the branch.
   - mem_redirect = late && (replay || (cond_late ^ in.pred_taken)).
   - mem_target = replay ? in.pc : in.alt_target.
   - MEM/WB gets, for a late branch:
     - rs1_val / rs2_val corrected from reg_q.read_data (for RVFI),
     - pc_next = cond_late ? branch_target : pc + 4,
     - valid = 0 on replay.
6. BHT write port. mem_stage registers:
   - bht_we_q <= in.valid && in.ctrl.is_branch
   - bht_widx_q <= in.pc[7:2]
   - bht_wdata_q <= late ? (cond_late ? inc(in.bht_ctr) : dec(in.bht_ctr)) : in.bht_upd
   It drives if_stage's existing write port. A branch sits in EX/MEM for exactly
   one cycle and killed slots arrive invalid, so there are no repeated or
   wrong-path writes.
7. core.sv.
   - redirect = ex_redirect || mem_redirect, with MEM (older) winning.
   - redirect_target = (is_jalr && !mem_redirect) ? jalr_sum
                      : (mem_redirect ? mem_target : alt_target).
     jalr_sum (fwd mux -> adder, the late arrival) stays at one mux level. The
     inner mux is registers plus the short MEM compare.
   - flush_if / flush_id use the combined redirect.
   - Build the final redirect gate as one expression so ABC folds mem_redirect
     into the existing (actual_taken ^ pred_taken) LUT instead of adding a level.
   - The hazard_unit comment "flush_id and ex_div_busy are never high together" no
     longer holds (a MEM redirect over a first-cycle divide). flush already has
     priority over hold in id_stage, and redirect over stall in pc_d, so update
     the comment.
8. RVFI-trap guard (seeds 1/3 limiter, RVFI-only).
   - Move the full-decoder is_illegal from mem_stage (EX/MEM.instr) to ex_stage:
     decoder(in.instr) -> new EX/MEM flop dec_ill. That path is ID/EX flops ->
     decoder -> flop, parallel to nothing late.
   - MEM then computes is_illegal = in.ctrl.is_illegal || in.dec_ill ||
     mem_misalign, 1-2 LUTs instead of 4 + MUX2_LUT6.
   - Bubbles carry garbage dec_ill but valid = 0, so rvfi_trap is unaffected.
   - Remove u_ill_dec from mem_stage.

  confirm ld_nz is really a flop, and that mem_redirect is merged into the redirect

- The replay path and the killed-divide abort are exercised by riscv-formal's

- RVFI stream in cosim should be byte-identical to the base except mem_rdata on

- About +45 FF, +250 LUT4.

lesson: - 2026-09-26 hyp-20260926-001-r14s0 (regression, -3.77%): Moving the RVFI-only full illegal decode one stage earlier (decoded in EX from ID/EX.instr and registered as EX/MEM.dec_ill, so MEM only ORs flops) kept cycles at 3,194,453 but cut the scored 3-seed median from 285.71 to 274.95 MHz (6 seeds 256.8-283.9, five of them below the base's 9-seed worst of 281.5), because moving a decode to another stage does not remove any of its ~4 LUT levels between flops: ABC9 merged the new EX decoder with div_unit's funct3 (is_unsigned) decode, which reads the same ID/EX.instr bits, giving a new ID/EX.data_q -> EX/MEM.reg_q path with 2.31 ns of logic on 3 of 6 seeds, and 2 more seeds still ended on the MEM misalign LUT that feeds both rvfi_trap and u_fwd.mem_wb_w_en's sync reset; the other variants did worse (full decode at the RVFI output from MEM/WB 224-272 MHz, a split opcode-only ID reg_write 213-270 MHz) because once the trap cone left, ABC9 re-mapped the co-critical imem -> decode -> ID/EX.reg_write_q cone deeper (2.66-2.77 vs 2.12 ns of logic); so a flop-to-flop decode only gets shorter if it is split across a register (e.g. register the funct/EBREAK match terms in ID/EX and combine them later), and removing one of several near-equal worst paths on this ~3.4 ns core just re-rolls the others, so it is not worth a slot on its own.

title: Late branch unit (v2 form): verify load-dependent BRANCHes in MEM, redirect one cycle later from flops
motivation:
Where the cycles go (r13s2's RVFI-trace replay of the current r12s1 core,
894.39 = 10 / 3,194,453 cycles x 285.71 MHz): 2,922,017 retirements, so
272,437 bubbles. Of these, 135,322 are load -> BRANCH load-use stalls,
59,353 load -> load, 51,852 BRANCH mispredicts (1 bubble each), 13,742 JALRs,
and 9,372 load -> ALU/store. nret=1 caps IPC at 1, so the cycle floor is 2.92M.
Load -> branch is the only large cycle lever left. The fetch-time BHT already
predicts 94.7% of those branches correctly (only 7,198 mispredict), so the
branch needs the loaded value only to verify its prediction.

Why this is the structural pick and not an Fmax restructure. I re-ran
synth + P&R on the base and reproduced 299.67 / 285.47 / 285.71 MHz exactly.
Seeds 1 and 3 end on EX/MEM.instr -> full illegal decode -> MEM/WB.is_illegal
(RVFI-only, 3.30 / 3.46 ns). Seed 2 ends on imem (LFSR) -> decode ->
ID/EX.reg_write_q (3.47 ns). Two throwaway probes show that Fmax-only edits
here are a lottery, not a lever:
  - Probe 1 only moved the trap decode behind MEM/WB (combinational to the
    untimed RVFI output). 6 seeds gave 211-270 MHz (median ~247). Every seed
    ended on the imem -> decode -> reg_write_q cone, which ABC9 re-mapped from
    4 to 6 cells.
  - Probe 2 also narrowed the ID/EX control half to opcode-only decodes and
    dropped the IF NOP mux. 6 seeds gave 122-172 MHz, on an EX compare carry
    chain -> 5 LUTs -> EX/MEM path at 5.8 ns.
The base's 285+ MHz is a favourable ABC9 roll of several ~3.5 ns cones. A
deterministic -3.8% cycle win is worth more than another re-roll.

Evidence for this exact form. r13s1 built this late branch on this same r12s1
base. Its v2 variant got the modelled cycles (3,194,453 -> ~3,073,600) with
a 9-seed Fmax median of 285.8 MHz (base 286.45). The scored seeds 1-3 came out
at 302 / 279 / 316. Unfortunately a later v3 overwrote v2 and was scored at
235 MHz. r13s2's combinational MEM-redirect form fell to 144-157 MHz. So the
fix is to rebuild v2 faithfully, with a hard stop.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a late branch unit: a conditional BRANCH that reads the rd of the LOAD
directly ahead of it skips the load-use stall. It is verified in MEM from
flops only. A mispredict is registered and redirects one cycle later, from
flops, through the existing redirect net. This is the v2 form of r13s1.

1. IF / hazard / ID.
   - if_id_t gains if_br = IF's existing pd_br predecode.
   - ID/EX's control half gains ld_nz_q = mem_read && rd != 0, so the final
     stall gate stays narrow.
   - load_use_hazard = ld_nz_q && (rd==rs1 || rd==rs2) && !if_br.
   - A late branch is late_dep = ld_nz_q && match && if_br && in.valid.
     ID/EX captures late_q = late_dep in the control half (reset/flush clear).
     It also captures is_branch_q <= dec_is_branch && !late_dep and
     pred_taken_q <= in.pred_taken && !late_dep, as D-input gating (v2).
     Do NOT move this to a sync reset (that was v3).
   - The real prediction travels in the data half as late_pred (data_q copy
     of pred_taken), together with bht_ctr, alt_target and imm.
   - In EX, the branch is then an inert non-branch: no EX redirect, no EX
     BHT write, no misalign trap.
2. EX. Derive late_rs1 = in.late && (fwd_rs1_sel == 2'd1), and late_rs2
   likewise: the LOAD sits in EX/MEM, so the forward unit already matches
   it (v2). Pass late, late_rs1/2, late_pred, branch_op, bht_ctr,
   alt_target and imm[1] into EX/MEM. EX/MEM.rs?_val/branch_target already
   exist. Add nothing to the ALU -> EX/MEM path.
3. MEM, the late compare, with flop operands only:
     a = late_rs1 ? MEM/WB.read_data : EX/MEM.rs1_val
     b = late_rs2 ? MEM/WB.read_data : EX/MEM.rs2_val
   The load is guaranteed to be in MEM/WB here, because hold_mem_wb only
   fires for a mem op in EX/MEM.
   cond is a six-way compare of (a, b). From it, register:
   - late_mis_q = EX/MEM.valid && late && !late_kill
                  && ((cond && !imm1) != late_pred)
   - late_tgt_q = EX/MEM.alt_target
   - MEM/WB: late_taken (cond && !imm1), late_trap (cond && imm1) and
     branch_target. Also MEM/WB.rs?_val <= late_rs? ? MEM/WB.read_data
     : rs?_val.
   - A 2-bit MEM BHT update: cond only selects between inc/dec counters
     precomputed from bht_ctr (never register the raw compare bit). It is
     registered and has priority over EX's registered write.
4. Redirect one cycle later, from flops only (late_kill = late_mis_q):
   - redirect = (actual_taken ^ pred_taken) | late_kill
   - redirect_target = late_kill ? late_tgt_q
                                 : (is_jalr ? jalr : alt_target)
   This reuses flush_if, flush_id, the IF NOP mux and pc_d unchanged.
   late_kill also clears, as flop-driven gating:
   - EX/MEM capture: valid, reg_write, mem_read, mem_write, late. This
     includes while stall_ex_mem is active.
   - MEM/WB capture: valid and reg_write.
   - The MEM-stage store: dmem_wen, st_done/post, cache update, and
     ex_mem_mem_op into dmem_stall.
   - div_unit gets a kill input -> IDLE, so a killed in-flight divide can
     never hand a stale DONE to a later DIV.
5. RVFI fix-ups at core.sv outputs, from registered bits (untimed):
   - pc_wdata = late_taken ? branch_target : pc_next
   - trap |= late_trap

Expected: cycles 3,194,453 -> ~3,073,600 (-3.8%), RVFI byte-identical apart
from cycle stamps. At unchanged Fmax, 10/3.0736M x 285.7 MHz = ~930 (+4%).
If seeds 1-3 land like r13s1's v2 (302/279/316), the score is ~980.

Implementation protocol (the last two builds failed on process, not on the
idea):
(a) Build v2 exactly as above. Pass lint, cocotb, formal (checks_si) and
    cosim. Then run P&R seeds 1-3 (about 1 minute each).
(b) If the seed 1-3 median is >= 280 MHz, commit and STOP. Do not chase a
    path that only a minority of seeds hit.
(c) Otherwise try only this: compute if_br from instr_word[6:2] == 5'b11000
    (no funct3 check; a reserved-funct3 late branch still traps via MEM's
    decode). Keep whichever tree has the better seed 1-3 median. Revert to
    the last formal-clean tree with more than 10 minutes left.
Never gate EX/MEM or MEM/WB D inputs with a same-cycle MEM signal
(r13s2). Keep the IF NOP mux and the MEM-stage illegal decode as they are
(probes 1 and 2 above).

lesson: - 2026-09-26 hyp-20260926-002-r14s1 (improvement, +9.93%): Rebuilding r13s1's v2 late branch faithfully on r12s1 (a load-dependent BRANCH skips the load-use stall and passes through EX as an inert op with is_branch_q/pred_taken_q cleared by D-input gating, MEM compares MEM/WB.read_data against EX/MEM.rs?_val using the forward unit's existing EX/MEM match, and a registered late_mis_q/late_tgt_q is ORed into EX's existing redirect one cycle later and kills EX/MEM, MEM/WB, the MEM store and div_unit) scored 983.24, right at the ~980 projected, which implies ~302 MHz at the modelled ~3.07M cycles (the median of v2's scored seeds in r13s1), so the -3.8% cycles came at no Fmax cost because the BHT already predicts 94.7% of these branches (135k skipped stalls cost only ~7.2k late mispredicts at ~2 extra bubbles each) and every new term reaches existing pipeline D inputs from a flop, unlike r13s2's same-cycle kill (144-157 MHz); so a verify-later speculation stays Fmax-neutral on this core as long as the new compare's operands and its kill/redirect are all registered, a variant already proven across several seeds can be rebuilt and banked with a "commit at seed 1-3 median >= 280 MHz, then stop" rule, and the next cycle levers (59k load->load stalls, 51.8k 1-bubble mispredicts) should be built the same way.

title: Speculate load-dependent branches on the BHT, verify in MEM, redirect one cycle later from a flop (r13s1 v2 form on r12s1, with trap-replay)
motivation:
r13s2 replayed the current core's RVFI trace (r12s1: 3,194,453 cycles, 2,922,017
retirements, so ~272k bubbles). The bubbles break down as:
  - load -> BRANCH load-use stalls   135,322 (49.7%)
  - load -> load                      59,353
  - BRANCH mispredicts (1 bubble)     51,852
  - JALR                              13,742
  - load -> ALU/store                  9,372
All other predictor levers are small on this trace:
  - bimodal 256 / 1024: -7.6k / -12k cycles
  - gshare: no better than bimodal-1024
  - a RAS: at most -13.7k
Each of those also adds logic on the BHT/pc_d fetch path. The big item is
the load -> branch stall. The fetch-time BHT already predicts every one of
those branches, 17 static sites (0x484/0x490/0x548/0x550 are ~28k each),
and gets 128,122 of 135,320 (94.7%) right. The loaded value is needed only
to verify the prediction, not to steer fetch.

History of this idea: it has landed its modelled cycles five times.
  - r5s2 / r7s2: beat their base cores, lost only to siblings.
  - r9s2 / r11s2: ABC9 re-mapped the ALU->EX/MEM adder. r12s1 has since
    hardened that adder into one 34-bit chain.
  - r13s2: the same-cycle MEM redirect gated EX/MEM D inputs and fell to
    144-157 MHz. The session ended broken.
  - r13s1: the registered-redirect form. Its "v2" build kept Fmax (9-seed
    median 285.8 vs base 286.45; seeds 1-3 were 302/279/316). It was scored
    as a regression only because a late v3 refactor overwrote it (235 MHz).
LESSONS says to re-apply exactly that v2 form on r12s1. No v2 RTL survives
in git, so this hypothesis re-specifies it. It also closes two correctness
gaps the earlier drafts left open:
  - A misaligned (trapping) load followed by a dependent late branch.
    riscv-formal's reg check requires the branch to see the OLD register
    value.
  - Wrong-path memory ops that now reach MEM. cosim flags any dmem_ren to an
    out-of-range address as oob.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
A conditional BRANCH that reads the rd of the LOAD directly ahead of it no
longer takes the load-use stall. It enters EX as an inert non-branch.
In MEM it is compared against the registered MEM/WB.read_data, and the
load is always in MEM/WB at that moment (lockstep argument below). A
mispredict is registered (late_kill_q, late_tgt_q) and folded into the
existing EX redirect one cycle later. No same-cycle MEM signal ever reaches
pc_d, the IF kill, or any ID/EX / EX/MEM D input.

Cost per event:
  - correct prediction: 0 bubbles (today 1)
  - mispredict: 3 bubbles (today 1 stall + 1 redirect = 2)
Model: 3,194,453 - 128,122 + 7,198 = 3,073,529 cycles (-3.79%). r13s1
measured 3,073,627. At the base 285.71 MHz that is ~929.6 fitness (+3.9%).

1. IF (if_stage). Export br_ok = pd_br && !pimm[1] on if_id_t. This is a
   valid-funct3 BRANCH whose target can never be misaligned, and IF already
   refuses to predict an imm[1] target. So a late branch can never trap in
   EX or MEM, and it needs no trap term.
   No kill gating is needed: on kill the IF instr is the NOP, whose
   rs1/rs2 = x0 can never match a load rd != 0.

2. hazard_unit + id_stage (ID/EX control half).
   - Add ld_nz_q = dec_mem_read && rd != 0, a control-half flop cleared on
     reset || flush. It replaces id_ex_mem_read and the 5-bit rd != 0 test
     (r7s2's trick), so the final gate stays small.
   - m = ld_nz_q && (id_ex_rd == if_rs1 || id_ex_rd == if_rs2).
   - load_use_hazard = m && !br_ok.
   - late = m && br_ok. It drives D inputs only, never a CE or sync clear.
   - The control half gains late_q. When late, capture is_branch_q = 0 and
     pred_taken_q = 0 (the v2 form). EX then sees a non-branch: no
     redirect, no BHT write, no misalign from the stale compare.
   - The data half keeps the real prediction and exports it as late_pred
     (data_q.pred_taken), with bht_ctr, alt_target and ctrl.branch_op.

3. ex_stage.
   - late_rs1 = in.late && fwd_rs1_sel == 2'd1, and likewise late_rs2 (the
     v2 form). The load is exactly EX/MEM when the branch is in EX, so
     forward_unit's EX/MEM match marks the late operand(s).
   - EX/MEM gains: late, late_rs1, late_rs2, late_pred, bht_ctr,
     alt_target. The existing branch_target already covers the RVFI fix.
   - late_kill (a flop from MEM):
     - redirect = (actual_taken ^ pred_taken) | late_kill. This is a spare
       LUT input.
     - redirect_target = late_kill ? late_tgt_q
                                   : (is_jalr ? jalr : alt_target).
       Every select is a flop, so this maps to a LUT5.
     - On late_kill, EX/MEM captures a bubble: valid, reg_write, mem_read,
       mem_write, is_branch, is_jump and late are 0. The data half is
       unchanged.
     - bht_we_q is also gated by !late_kill. Both inputs are flops.

4. mem_stage, the late unit. It uses only flops and ends only in flops.
   - Operands:
       a = late_rs1 ? MEM/WB.read_data : EX/MEM.rs1_val
       b = late_rs2 ? MEM/WB.read_data : EX/MEM.rs2_val
   - Six-way compare on ctrl.branch_op gives cond.
   - lv     = in.valid && in.late && !late_kill
   - replay = lv && !MEM/WB.ctrl.reg_write
     The load ahead trapped (misaligned), so read_data is not
     architectural.
   - Registered:
       late_kill_q <= lv && (replay || (cond != late_pred))
       late_tgt_q  <= replay ? EX/MEM.pc : EX/MEM.alt_target
     On replay the branch is killed and refetched. It then re-executes
     normally, because the load has already retired.
   - MEM/WB:
       valid     <= in.valid && !late_kill && !replay
       reg_write is cleared on late_kill
       late_taken <= lv && cond                      (1 bit, RVFI only)
       late_tgt  <= EX/MEM.branch_target             (RVFI only)
       rs?_val   <= late_rs? ? MEM/WB.read_data : in.rs?_val
     so RVFI rs?_rdata is exact.
   - BHT: bht_late_wdata_q <= cond ? inc(bht_ctr) : dec(bht_ctr). The
     counters are precomputed from flops, so the compare only selects
     (r7s2 lesson: never register the raw compare bit). Also register
     bht_late_we_q <= lv && !replay, and the index from EX/MEM.pc.
   - Wrong-path MEM op on late_kill: ld and st are gated with !late_kill.
     That covers dmem_ren (cosim oob on a garbage address), dmem_wen, the
     store-buffer post, ld_fill / cache update and mem_ready, and
     ex_mem_mem_op into dmem_stall is gated too. Otherwise dmem_stall
     would suppress flush_id. With ready=1 this is just one AND from a
     flop on dmem_wen / dmem_ren.

5. div_unit gets a kill input (late_kill) that forces state_q to ST_IDLE,
   and kill wins over start. A wrong-path DIV can be the first or second
   instruction behind the late branch; without the kill it would leave a
   stale DONE result for the next DIV.

6. core.sv.
   - Merge the BHT writes: the MEM late write has priority over EX's
     registered write. Both are flops, and a dropped EX write is only a
     lost hint.
   - RVFI: io_rvfi_pc_wdata_0 = mem_wb.late_taken ? mem_wb.late_tgt
     : mem_wb.pc_next. This is the same mux depth as rd_wdata, and the
     RVFI outputs only feed the untimed led XOR in core_bench_si.

Lockstep argument, which the implementer should restate in comments:
  - ID/EX captures only when EX/MEM advances, since hold_id is dmem_stall
    or div_busy and a divide is never a load.
  - EX/MEM never holds a branch, because dmem_stall needs a mem op.
  So when the late branch is in MEM, MEM/WB is exactly its load with
  valid = 1.

Known residual risk: at cycle t the wrong-path instruction in EX (for
example a JALR) may still redirect for one cycle before late_kill wins at
t+1. In CoreMark those targets are return addresses, which are in range;
r13s1 passed cosim with the same shape. Only if cosim reports imem oob,
hold a JALR in EX while EX/MEM.late is set.

Process (from r13s1/r13s2):
  - Build exactly this v2 form first and run formal + cosim + 3-seed P&R.
  - Commit it as the reference.
  - Do not move the late clears onto sync-reset pins, and never gate EX/MEM
    D inputs with a same-cycle MEM signal.
  - Do not chase a path that only a minority of seeds hit.
  - Replace the tree only with a variant whose multi-seed P&R beats it.
  - Revert to the last formal-clean tree before investigating any loss.
  - If a majority of seeds end on the new imem -> hazard -> late /
    is_branch_q D term, the one sanctioned fallback is: keep is_branch_q /
    pred_taken_q unchanged and gate in EX, with
      redirect = ((actual ^ pred) && !in.late) | late_kill
    and the BHT write && !in.late.

changes.description: if_id_t: add br_ok. id_ex_t: add late, ld_nz, late_pred. ex_mem_t: add late, late_rs1, late_rs2, late_pred, bht_ctr[1:0], alt_target[31:0]. mem_wb_t: add late_taken and late_tgt[31:0] for the RVFI pc_wdata fixup.

Export br_ok = pd_br && !pimm[1] (for BRANCH, pimm[1] = instr_word[8]) on the IF/ID bundle. Nothing else changes: the late redirect arrives through the existing redirect/redirect_target inputs (redirect already beats stall).

Replace id_ex_mem_read + rd!=0 with the registered id_ex_ld_nz. load_use_hazard = ld_nz && (rd==rs1 || rd==rs2) && !br_ok. New output late = ld_nz && match && br_ok (D input only). New input late_kill: OR it into the redirect term of flush_if/flush_id, and gate ex_mem_mem_op with !late_kill in dmem_stall.

Control half: add late_q and ld_nz_q (dec_mem_read && rd != 0), cleared on reset||flush. When late, capture is_branch_q = 0 and pred_taken_q = 0. Data half: export the real pred_taken as late_pred (bht_ctr, alt_target and branch_op are already there).

late_rs1/late_rs2 = in.late && fwd_rs?_sel == 1. Carry late*, late_pred, bht_ctr and alt_target into EX/MEM. New inputs late_kill / late_tgt: redirect |= late_kill, redirect_target = late_kill ? late_tgt : (is_jalr ? jalr : alt_target). On late_kill, EX/MEM captures a bubble (valid/reg_write/mem_read/mem_write/is_branch/is_jump/late = 0). bht_we_q gated by !late_kill. Pass late_kill to div_unit as kill.

Late branch unit. Flop-only operands (MEM/WB.read_data or EX/MEM.rs?_val by late_rs?) feed a six-way compare. Replay when the load ahead trapped (MEM/WB.ctrl.reg_write == 0). Registered outputs: late_kill_q, late_tgt_q (replay ? pc : alt_target), the BHT late write (index, cond-selected precomputed inc/dec, we), and MEM/WB late_taken / late_tgt / substituted rs?_val. MEM/WB.valid is cleared on late_kill or replay, and reg_write on late_kill. ld/st are gated by !late_kill, so a wrong-path MEM op issues no dmem_ren/dmem_wen, store post, cache fill or stall.
Add a kill input that forces state_q to ST_IDLE in both the real and ALTOPS sequences, with priority over start, so a wrong-path divide flushed by late_kill cannot leave a stale DONE result.

Wire br_ok, late, ld_nz, late_kill and late_tgt between IF/hazard/ID/EX/MEM. Merge the MEM late BHT write (priority) with EX's registered write onto IF's single BHT port. RVFI pc_wdata = mem_wb.late_taken ? mem_wb.late_tgt : mem_wb.pc_next.

Add programs checking final register/memory state (and cycle count where noted): LW + dependent BEQ/BNE, predicted-correct (no stall) and mispredicted in both directions; a late mispredict with a SW right behind the branch (must not reach dmem) and with a LW to an out-of-range address behind it (no dmem_ren); a late mispredict with a DIV one and two instructions behind (no stale result on a later DIV); a misaligned LW followed by a dependent branch (replay: the branch sees the old value); a load-dependent branch under dmem backpressure.

lesson: - 2026-09-26 hyp-20260926-003-r14s2 (regression, +0.18%): The same flop-only v2 late load->branch that scored +9.93% as sibling r14s1 scored only 896.04 here (about 275 MHz if it landed the modelled ~3.07M cycles, against r14s1's ~302), and the biggest change in its diff outside the hypothesis moved the RVFI-only full illegal decode from MEM (EX/MEM.instr, where r12s1 and r14s1 keep it) to a second decoder on MEM/WB.instr at the rvfi_trap output, the placement r14s0 (224-272 MHz) and r14s1's probe 1 (211-270 MHz, imem -> decode -> ID/EX.reg_write_q re-mapped from 4 to 6 cells) had already measured as an Fmax loss, so the likely cause is that side change rather than the late branch or its flop-only additions (trap-replay on a misaligned load, !late_kill on dmem_ren/wen, a div_unit kill); when rebuilding a design with multi-seed P&R behind it, leave every unrelated cone, especially the RVFI trap decode, exactly where the proven build had it.
